newsitem.title: INDIA: Price containment beneficial to exports - India RBI.
newsitem.headline: Price containment beneficial to exports - India RBI.

text.p: India's central bank governor told exporters on Friday that containment of domestic price increase has the same beneficial impact as depreciation of the nominal exchange rate.

"With capital inflows, the natural tendency is for the domestic currency to appreciate," Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor Chakravarty Rangarajan told a meeting of the Indian Engineering Export Promotion Council (EEPC).
He said a currency's appreciation could be prevented only if the central bank intervened and bought the excess supply of the foreign currency at the prevailing rate.
"The consequent accretion to reserves will however lead to an expansion in money supply," the governor said.

"Thus, exchange rate management will have to balance the needs of the exporters to have a favourable exchange rate and the need to prevent monetary expansion from going beyond what is considered appropriate for maintaining price stability."
"Exporters also need to understand that containment of domestic price increase has the same beneficial effect as the depreciation of the nominal exchange rate," he said.

"If the nominal exchange rate is stabilised at a certain level by letting the foreign exchange assets of the central bank to increase, it may have an adverse effect on the exporters through price increase arising from more than the desired increase arising from more than the desired increase in money supply," he said.

"There can therefore be no rigid formula governing exchange rate determination. Monetary authorities need continually to perform a balancing act between ensuring an exchange rate which will be supportive of exports and the need to contain monetary expansion within reasonable limits."
